name: pulse-dot-soft
concept: A single dot grows and glows slightly in a slow, even rhythm. Use it for a calm status indicator that shows quiet, ongoing activity.

name: pulse-dot-sharp
concept: A dot snaps outward fast, then eases back. Use it where activity is brisk, such as a live-update marker or an active recording light.

name: pulse-dot-slow
concept: A dot swells gradually and holds before easing back down. Use it for background work that is running but not urgent.

name: heartbeat-pulse
concept: A dot beats twice quickly, like lub-dub, then rests before repeating. Use it for a health check, a vitals monitor, or any alive-and-well signal.

name: pulse-fade-dot
concept: A dot dims and brightens on a steady loop with no size change. Use it as a subtle activity light where movement would be distracting.

name: pulse-grow-hold
concept: A dot expands and holds at its largest size for a beat before snapping back. Use it for a loading cue with a distinct pause of emphasis.

name: pulse-blur-dot
concept: A dot grows while briefly going out of focus, then sharpens back. Use it for a dreamy or processing feel, like a camera hunting for focus.

name: pulse-glow-dot
concept: A dot brightens like a light source as it grows, then dims back. Use it for a beacon-like status light that suggests power or signal.

name: sonar-ping
concept: A dot expands outward while fading to nothing, then resets to repeat. Use it for a scanning or searching cue, like a radar sweep.

name: sonar-ping-tight
concept: A faster, smaller ping that expands and fades in quick bursts. Use it for a compact scanning indicator in a dense interface.

name: squash-pulse-dot
concept: A dot squashes wide then stretches tall on a steady loop, like it is breathing sideways. Use it for a playful, elastic loading cue.

name: ball-bounce-basic
concept: A single ball hops up and lands with a light squash, arcade-loading-screen style. Use it as a friendly, game-like wait indicator.

name: ball-bounce-squash
concept: A ball rises, falls, and flattens hard on landing before popping back round. Use it where extra squash-and-stretch character fits the brand.

name: ball-bounce-double
concept: A ball bounces twice in quick succession, then rests before repeating. Use it as a distinctive loading rhythm that reads as counting.

name: ball-bounce-triple
concept: A ball takes three shrinking hops before settling and starting over. Use it for a bouncing-to-a-stop feel on each loop cycle.

name: ball-bounce-wobble
concept: A ball bounces upward while rocking slightly side to side. Use it for a lively, slightly clumsy loading character.

name: ball-bounce-low
concept: A ball makes a short, quick hop close to the ground. Use it for a compact loading indicator in a small space.

name: ball-bounce-high
concept: A ball launches high with a moment of hang time at the top before dropping and squashing. Use it for a bold, attention-grabbing loader.

name: ball-bounce-fade
concept: A ball rises and dims near the top of its arc, then returns and brightens on landing. Use it to suggest the ball leaving and returning to view.

name: ball-drop-squash
concept: A ball starts raised, drops straight down, and squashes flat on impact before resetting to the top. Use it for a one-way falling loading cue.

name: ball-hop-lean
concept: A ball hops upward while leaning into the motion, then straightens on landing. Use it for a loader with a sense of forward energy.

name: bar-pulse-height
concept: A bar stretches taller from its base and settles back on a steady loop. Use it for a single-bar activity meter, like a compact level indicator.

name: bar-pulse-fade
concept: A bar grows taller while dimming slightly, then returns to rest and full brightness. Use it for a softer variant of a single-bar activity meter.

name: bar-fill-snap
concept: A bar fills from empty to full, then snaps instantly back to empty and repeats. Use it for a repeating fill cue distinct from a sweeping progress bar.

name: bar-drain-reset
concept: A full bar drains down to empty, then snaps instantly back to full and repeats. Use it for a countdown-like loading cue, the reverse of a fill bar.

name: bar-tick-step
concept: A bar fills in three distinct steps rather than a smooth sweep, then snaps back to start. Use it for a loader that reads as counting progress.

name: ring-breathe
concept: A ring shape grows and shrinks gently in place, like slow breathing. Use it for a calm loading ring that is not spinning.

name: ring-pulse-glow
concept: A ring brightens and grows slightly as it pulses, then dims back. Use it for a loading ring that suggests energy building and releasing.

name: ring-expand-fade
concept: A ring expands outward and fades at its widest, then contracts and returns to full opacity. Use it for a ring that breathes out and back in.

name: hourglass-tilt
concept: An element tilts gently side to side while narrowing at its middle, like sand settling in an hourglass. Use it for a slow, waiting-in-progress cue.

name: hourglass-flip
concept: An element rotates a full turn slowly while shrinking through the middle of the flip. Use it for a deliberate, unhurried waiting indicator.

name: cursor-blink-scale
concept: An element blinks on and off sharply, with a slight vertical shrink when hidden, like a text cursor waiting for input. Use it for a typing-ready cue.

name: thinking-breathe
concept: An element swells and softens very slowly, calmer and quieter than a typing indicator. Use it for a system that is thinking before it responds.

name: thinking-drift
concept: An element drifts up slightly while growing, then settles back down. Use it for an idle, contemplative loading cue with a hint of motion.

name: orbit-dot-pulse
concept: A dot shifts side to side while shrinking slightly at each extreme, suggesting a small orbit. Use it for a compact, self-contained loading cue.

name: blip-pulse
concept: A dot sits dim, then flashes bright and large in a quick blip before returning to rest. Use it for a radar-style, periodic activity signal.

name: beacon-pulse
concept: A dot rests dim for most of the loop, then briefly flashes bright and slightly larger like a lighthouse beacon. Use it for a low-frequency status signal.

name: stretch-pulse-vertical
concept: An element stretches tall then returns to its normal height on a steady loop, with no horizontal change. Use it for a simple vertical activity cue.

name: stretch-pulse-horizontal
concept: An element stretches wide then returns to its normal width on a steady loop, with no vertical change. Use it for a simple horizontal activity cue.

name: pulse-rock
concept: An element rocks side to side while growing slightly at each extreme. Use it for a loading cue with a gentle rocking character.

name: pulse-tilt-shift
concept: An element lifts slightly and tilts while dimming, then settles back level and opaque. Use it for a loading cue with a small sense of lift.

name: double-bounce-pause
concept: An element bounces twice in quick succession, the second hop shorter than the first, then pauses before repeating. Use it for a distinctive counted bounce.

name: micro-bounce-loop
concept: An element makes small, quick hops back to back with no pause between them. Use it for a busy, rapid loading rhythm.

name: bounce-settle
concept: An element bounces up once, then wobbles smaller and smaller before coming to rest, and repeats. Use it for a loader that reads as settling into place.

name: pulse-expand-contract
concept: An element grows and shrinks through a wide size range with no opacity change. Use it where a bold, visible pulse is needed against a busy background.

name: pulse-veil
concept: An element nearly disappears and reappears, with only a slight size change alongside the opacity swing. Use it for an opacity-led loading cue.

name: pulse-dim-bright
concept: An element swings from dim to bright and back using brightness alone, with only a small opacity shift. Use it for a light-emitting loading cue.

name: pulse-soft-blur-fade
concept: An element softens out of focus while fading, then sharpens back to full opacity, with no size change. Use it for a hazy, processing-in-progress cue.

name: loader-blob-pulse
concept: An element morphs unevenly between wide and tall on each phase of the loop, like a soft blob wobbling. Use it for a playful, organic loading shape.

name: loader-pip-bounce
concept: A small element hops up while brightening, then drops back and dims, in a tight, quick loop. Use it as a minimal loading pip for compact spaces.
